proof.criterion: A1c: envoy-listener serves on an inherited socket, refuses a bad one with no fallback bind, and its auth fence judges the socket's real address
proof.surface: pod, real envoy-listener built at the head, a real nats-server on an OS-chosen port, a throwaway Python driver that hands it each kind of descriptor as fd 3
proof.command: TBIN=<bin> TNATS=nats://127.0.0.1:<port> PODIP=<pod ip> python3 $TMPDIR/tester/fdmatrix.py listener
proof.observed: A loopback v4 socket, and a v4-mapped ::ffff:127.0.0.1 socket on AF_INET6, serve: /healthz answers 200, the log names the socket's address, and only one descriptor in the process names the listening inode (the raw fd 3 is closed and its number is reused). These are refused with exit 1 and the variable named: 0.0.0.0, the pod IP, :: and ::ffff:0.0.0.0 sockets without credentials ('ENVOY_API_TOKEN or … is required when ENVOY_LISTEN_FD=3, a socket listening on …, is not on loopback'), UDP, unix, bound-not-listening, connected, a regular file, a closed fd, fd 2, "", "+3", " 3", ENVOY_LISTEN_HOST=localhost, and PORT=0. A wildcard socket serves with ENVOY_API_TOKEN set or with ENVOY_API_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED=1.
proof.negativeControl: inherited 0.0.0.0 socket, no credentials → exit 1: 'ENVOY_API_TOKEN or the ENVOY_OIDC_ISSUER/ENVOY_OIDC_AUDIENCE pair is required when ENVOY_LISTEN_FD=3, a socket listening on 0.0.0.0:56873, is not on loopback'

proof.criterion: S3: the Dispatch Playwright harness serves on OS-chosen ports through e2e/run.ts, and refuses without it
proof.surface: pod, Chromium via bun e2e/run.ts, scratch pgvector databases
proof.command: two `bun e2e/run.ts -- bunx playwright test --config e2e/playwright.config.ts --project=chromium --output <own dir> e2e/smoke.e2e.ts e2e/external-links.e2e.ts e2e/claim.e2e.ts` at once; bare `bunx playwright test`; DISPATCH_E2E_PORT=<held>; SIGTERM to run.ts at 0.3/1/2 s
proof.observed: Both harnesses came up on 10 different ports and passed 4 rows each. A bare run is refused: 'The Dispatch e2e harness is not running … run it through e2e/run.ts'.
